text: This is where the toolkit stops being a plan and starts being code: a module of gate matrices, and a handful of small functions that build a state vector and apply gates to it correctly, the foundation everything in Lesson 24 will sit on top of.

gates dot p y holds the fixed, minimal gate set, identity, Pauli-X, Hadamard, and CNOT, as NumPy arrays. apply_gate and apply_gates chain operations correctly, left to right in time. kron_gate extends a single-qubit gate to a multi-qubit system using the Kronecker product from Chapter 2, just packaged as a named, reusable function. And verifying each step by hand against a known fact is what catches a bug like accidentally swapping which qubit Hadamard acts on.

The gate set is four lines: identity, Pauli-X, Hadamard scaled by one over root two, and the four-by-four CNOT matrix. kron_gate of H and I builds the matrix that applies Hadamard to qubit zero while leaving qubit one alone, exactly as covered back in Chapter 2.

Starting from the all-zero state, one, zero, zero, zero, applying H tensor I gives point seven zero seven one, zero, point seven zero seven one, zero, confirmed by hand: qubit zero is in superposition, qubit one is still definitely zero. Applying CNOT next moves the ket-one-zero component to ket-one-one, because CNOT flips the target exactly when the control is one, landing on the Bell state, point seven zero seven one, zero, zero, point seven zero seven one.
Next lesson adds the two things that make this toolkit actually interpretable: computing real measurement probabilities and sampling outcomes from them, plus plotting the result.
